learningObjectives: Explain why a project-specific safety plan is needed.
Identify the activities and evidence controlled by the plan.
concept: A safety plan defines how functional-safety activities will be performed, reviewed, tracked and evidenced for a specific development.
It connects lifecycle obligations with project milestones, responsibilities, supplier deliveries and release criteria.
whyItMatters: Without an actively maintained safety plan, technical work can become disconnected from required evidence, dependencies and confirmation measures.
automotiveExample: For an integrated brake and ESC controller, the plan coordinates HARA updates, architecture reviews, supplier evidence, fault-injection milestones and release readiness across vehicle variants.
commonMistakes: Treating the plan as a one-time document
Failing to update the plan after a major change
